system:
You draft public warning messages for a national alerting authority.
You receive event inputs (each marked verified or unverified) and the issuing context.
Write one alert in English as CAP 1.2 fields.

- Use only facts present in the verified inputs. Do not add places, numbers, times or hazards that are not there.
- Leave unverified inputs out of the alert, and say why in `left_out`.
- `description` is the text shown on the phone by cell broadcast: plain words, under 280 characters, hazard + where + until when, if known.
- `instruction` is the protective action in one or two short sentences.
- Pick CAP values honestly: status from the context (Actual for a real event, Exercise for a drill), severity and urgency from the inputs.
- `note_for_reviewer` is one or two sentences for the human approver: what you were unsure about.
user:
Issuer: Demo national authority (stands in for the real issuer)
Context: real event
Target area (chosen by the operator): Eastern, southern and western areas (demo zone)

Event inputs:
1. [verified; NCM via WAM, 2026-08-22, https://www.wam.ae/en/article/c1v24bo-ncm-forecasts-light-heavy-rain-across-several-uae] ABU DHABI, 22nd August, 2026 (WAM) -- The National Centre of Meteorology (NCM) issued an alert over the possibility of convective cloud formation accompanied by light to moderate rainfall, which may become heavy at times. The alert is in effect from 13:30 on Saturday until 21:00 the same day. The NCM said the weather conditions are expected to affect some eastern, southern and western areas, extending to parts of the country's interior.
2. [verified; issuer profile] Issuer public site (demo): https://alerts.example.ae
3. [verified; institution reviewers] Objections from the institution reviewers to your previous draft. Fix what is within the verified inputs; do not add facts: Network operator and regulator reviewer objects (phone_text): Neither the English nor the Arabic phone text tells the public what to do. The first page carries only the hazard description and no protective action, which fails the first-page hazard-and-action check. Fix: Add a short protective action to both languages, immediately after the hazard so it falls on page 1. For example: 'NCM alert: heavy rain possible – avoid valleys and flood-prone areas, drive carefully.' Add the Arabic equivalent early in the text, since UCS-2 pages hold only 41 characters. Keep both texts under 15 pages. [cites Wireless Emergency Alerts; Amendments to Part 11, Report and Order (DA 25-12), multilingual WEA templates, p.21]

data.headline: NCM alert: rain, heavy at times, possible in eastern, southern and western areas, Saturday 13:30 to 21:00
data.description: NCM alert: heavy rain possible. Avoid valleys and flood-prone areas, drive carefully. Convective clouds with light to moderate rain, heavy at times, in some eastern, southern and western areas and parts of the interior, Sat 22 Aug, 13:30 to 21:00.
data.instruction: Avoid valleys and flood-prone areas, and drive carefully. Follow updates at https://alerts.example.ae.
left_out: No unverified inputs were received, so nothing was excluded on that basis.
Arabic phone text was not drafted because this task asks for one alert in English. The reviewer's Arabic fix, with the protective action early in the text, still needs a separate Arabic draft.
data.note_for_reviewer: The protective action is the wording the network and regulator reviewer suggested. The NCM report itself gives no protective advice, so please confirm the wording is acceptable. I chose severity Moderate and urgency Expected because NCM describes rain that is possible and may be heavy at times, starting at 13:30. Please confirm these values.
